Global permutation test of condition separation (PERMANOVA)

Source: R/quant-stats.R
permanova_condition.Rd

Answers "do the conditions separate at all?" before any per-feature claim is made, using the distance-based pseudo-F of Anderson (2001): the ratio of between-group to within-group sums of squared Euclidean distances between samples, with a permutation null obtained by shuffling the condition labels. It is non-parametric, makes no distributional assumption, and needs no extra package. Only features quantified in every column are used, since a distance must be computed on a common feature set.

Usage

permanova_condition(mat, coldata, n_perm = 999, seed = 1234)

Arguments

mat

Numeric matrix of (normalized, optionally imputed) log2 intensities, features x units.

coldata

Column metadata from build_quant_matrix().

n_perm

Number of label permutations. Default 999.

seed

Random seed. Default 1234.

Value

A list with F (pseudo-F), p_value, n_perm, n_features (complete features used) and n_groups; NULL with a warning when fewer than two groups or no complete features are available.

Details

The permutation p-value is bounded below by the number of distinct label assignments: a 3-vs-3 comparison admits only choose(6, 3) / 2 = 10 of them, so its smallest attainable p-value is about 0.1, however clean the separation. Read the pseudo-F alongside the p-value in small designs.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
permanova_condition(mat_n, qm$coldata)
} # }
